You're doing a single, continuous, hands-on Playwright walkthrough of a real customer journey against the STAGING environment of the Nxeon "Nexion" v2 hosting-platform portal, at http://51.79.162.96:8080 (reachable directly by IP:port — no domain/TLS needed). This is a real Next.js app with a real backend and a real (separate, staging-only) Postgres DB. Provisioning/payment provider calls are sandboxed (NXEON_SANDBOX=1) so no real VM gets created and no real card gets charged, but every application code path — auth, DB writes, order/pricing logic, session handling — is real production code, not a mockup.

WHY THIS MATTERS: this staging deploy is the last verification gate before this portal redesign gets promoted to actual production. Every individual page/feature has already been audited and fixed piecemeal by other passes today. Your job is different: walk through ONE continuous, realistic customer session end-to-end, exactly as a brand-new real customer would, to catch anything that only breaks at the SEAMS between steps (e.g., session/auth state not surviving a step transition, a value computed at signup not showing up correctly three steps later, a redirect going somewhere wrong after an action). Don't just spot-check individual pages in isolation — go through them in the realistic sequence a real person would, using outputs from each step (verification codes, order IDs, account info) as inputs to the next, the way a real user's browser state would carry forward.

THE JOURNEY, IN ORDER:
1. **Register** a brand-new account from scratch at /register (or wherever the real sign-up flow is — find it) with a fresh, unique test email (e.g. `nx-e2e-<random>@example.com`) and a real password. Use whatever the real form requires.
2. **Verify the account** — this app has a real email-verification step. Since this is a sandboxed backend, the verification email won't actually send via SMTP; find out how verification actually completes in this environment (check the DB directly if needed — you have shell access, or look for a dev/testing bypass already documented in the codebase at /opt/nxeon-v2, e.g. search for how other test/audit scripts have handled this today) — do not skip verification or treat an unverified account as good enough; a real customer verifies before they can do anything meaningful, so confirm this step for real.
3. **Log in** as this brand new, now-verified account (not as the pre-seeded admin account used in other passes).
4. **Deploy a service** — go through the deploy wizard for real, pick ANY one product (VPS, game server, hosting, or email — your choice, pick whichever seems most representative), select a plan and term, and get all the way to a real order placement/checkout confirmation. Since this is sandboxed, actual provisioning won't happen, but the ORDER should genuinely get created (job row, service row, wallet/charge record — whatever this app's real order flow produces).
5. **Pay** — go through whatever real payment/checkout step exists for this order (sandboxed card charge is fine — the point is exercising the real checkout code path, not an actual Stripe charge).
6. **Manage the service** — after the order completes, navigate to My Services / the dashboard, find the newly-created service, and open its detail/management page. Check that it actually appears (not just in a "pending" ghost state that never resolves), and that basic management actions on its page (whatever's real and safe to click — e.g. viewing its settings, its metrics tab, renaming it) don't error out.
7. **Cancel** — find and use the real cancellation flow for this service, and confirm it actually transitions to a cancelled state (check the DB or the UI reflecting "cancelled"/"terminated" afterward), not just a client-side illusion.

Take a screenshot after each major step. Note every console error, hydration warning, network 4xx/5xx, or visibly broken UI you hit along the way, even if it doesn't block progress. If a step is fundamentally blocked (can't verify, can't check out, etc.), don't fake your way past it — stop, document exactly what blocked you and why, and report that as a finding rather than skipping ahead.

Do NOT fix anything — this is a verification-only pass. Do not fabricate results. Playwright scripts must live inside /opt/nxeon-v2 for module resolution (any subdirectory), delete them when done. Save screenshots to /tmp/claude-0/-/a847f019-50a6-4b60-bcba-1133f2a3ca8a/scratchpad/e2e-*.png.

Report back with a clear PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict for each of the 7 steps, and a concise overall verdict on whether this journey completed cleanly end-to-end. Keep the report under 600 words, structured step-by-step.

content.content: # Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server — mistakes here are not sandboxed.** The `db` subcommand refusing obvious writes is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary; the access itself is full root. **Update, 2026-09-12: the owner authorized this session to build, deploy, and promote the Nexion portal to production directly from here** — including running `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` and `scripts/promote-production.sh` on node-1, and writing to the prod DB as those scripts require (`prisma db push --accept-data-loss` on the way to production is the expected, sanctioned behavior of that script, not a mistake to avoid). This supersedes the "treat it as read-only, ask first" rule that used to sit here — the routine build/deploy/promote path no longer needs a stop-and-ask. That authorization carries guardrails that are **not optional**: - **Take a fresh, named `pg_dump` snapshot immediately before any write to the prod DB**, the same discipline already used for the pre-merge backup (`pre--.dump` under `/root/db-backups` on node-1, pulled down to node-2 too). Never skip this because a daily timer already ran — the daily timer isn't synced to the moment you're about to change something. - **Stop and report before proceeding if a step turns out more destructive or irreversible than expected** — e.g. `prisma db push --accept-data-loss` reporting it would actually drop a column or table rather than just add one, a schema change that isn't purely additive, or anything that would disrupt a customer mid-session in a way the sanctioned scripts don't already account for. "Automatic" covers the routine, expected path; it does not mean an unexpected destructive step gets waved through. - **Anything outside the build/deploy/promote workflow is still stop-and-ask** — touching customer credentials, hand-editing `/opt/nxeon` outside the sanctioned scripts, restarting a service those scripts don't themselves restart, or touching any of the `/opt/nxeon-*` siblings that belong to other sessions. The authorization is for shipping this fork to production, not a blanket lift of every caution on this box. ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run a manual, ad hoc build in `/opt/nxeon`.** Clobbering its `.next` with a raw `npm run build` has taken the admin panel down before. Running the sanctioned `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Reaching node-1" above) is fine — it exists specifically to update production without that failure mode; improvising your own build command in that directory is not. 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and before spending on any paid third-party tool. 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 8. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file. ## Verification discipline A change is not done until it is **deployed and screenshotted**. There is a login-and-capture script: ```bash node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/directory /dashboard/settings # defaults to the design customer account; override with NX_EMAIL / NX_PASS ``` Playwright scripts must live inside `/opt/nxeon-v2` so the module resolves. Read the PNG back and actually look at it — a sliced game wordmark, a clipped top bar and an empty Mods tab were all invisible in the code and obvious in a screenshot. ## Things that have already cost hours here - **Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls.** Always `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && …`. - **`git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks.** Write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`. - **`git bundle create f A..B` with two raw SHAs** makes a bundle with no refs, which git refuses as empty. The tip must be a named ref: `A..design/v2`. - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` aurora layer paints above static content.** Page content needs `relative z-[1]`. - **A `backdrop-filter` ancestor becomes the containing block for `fixed` children** — `createPortal` to `document.body` instead. - **Never size a fixed overlay from a header's height.** That is the header's bottom edge only when nothing sits above it, and the sandbox banner does. Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`.

#     restart a prod service, never build in /opt/nxeon (its .next is being
#     served; clobbering it has taken the admin panel down before).
#   * Never `pkill -f` by pattern over there.
#   * If you need to CHANGE something on node-1, stop and ask first.
#
# Quoting through two levels of ssh is where this goes wrong, so the subcommands
# below exist to keep callers out of it.
#
#   scripts/node1.sh db "select count(*) from \"Card\""   # read-only query
#   scripts/node1.sh board <cardId>                       # list a card's files
#   scripts/node1.sh pull <cardId> [dest]                 # copy a card's files here

content.content: # Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server — mistakes here are not sandboxed.** The `db` subcommand refusing obvious writes is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary; the access itself is full root. **Update, 2026-09-12: the owner authorized this session to build, deploy, and promote the Nexion portal to production directly from here** — including running `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` and `scripts/promote-production.sh` on node-1, and writing to the prod DB as those scripts require (`prisma db push --accept-data-loss` on the way to production is the expected, sanctioned behavior of that script, not a mistake to avoid). This supersedes the "treat it as read-only, ask first" rule that used to sit here — the routine build/deploy/promote path no longer needs a stop-and-ask. That authorization carries guardrails that are **not optional**: - **Take a fresh, named `pg_dump` snapshot immediately before any write to the prod DB**, the same discipline already used for the pre-merge backup (`pre--.dump` under `/root/db-backups` on node-1, pulled down to node-2 too). Never skip this because a daily timer already ran — the daily timer isn't synced to the moment you're about to change something. - **Stop and report before proceeding if a step turns out more destructive or irreversible than expected** — e.g. `prisma db push --accept-data-loss` reporting it would actually drop a column or table rather than just add one, a schema change that isn't purely additive, or anything that would disrupt a customer mid-session in a way the sanctioned scripts don't already account for. "Automatic" covers the routine, expected path; it does not mean an unexpected destructive step gets waved through. - **Anything outside the build/deploy/promote workflow is still stop-and-ask** — touching customer credentials, hand-editing `/opt/nxeon` outside the sanctioned scripts, restarting a service those scripts don't themselves restart, or touching any of the `/opt/nxeon-*` siblings that belong to other sessions. The authorization is for shipping this fork to production, not a blanket lift of every caution on this box. ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run a manual, ad hoc build in `/opt/nxeon`.** Clobbering its `.next` with a raw `npm run build` has taken the admin panel down before. Running the sanctioned `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Reaching node-1" above) is fine — it exists specifically to update production without that failure mode; improvising your own build command in that directory is not. 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and before spending on any paid third-party tool. 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 8. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file. ## Verification discipline A change is not done until it is **deployed and screenshotted**. There is a login-and-capture script: ```bash node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/directory /dashboard/settings # defaults to the design customer account; override with NX_EMAIL / NX_PASS ``` Playwright scripts must live inside `/opt/nxeon-v2` so the module resolves. Read the PNG back and actually look at it — a sliced game wordmark, a clipped top bar and an empty Mods tab were all invisible in the code and obvious in a screenshot. ## Things that have already cost hours here - **Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls.** Always `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && …`. - **`git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks.** Write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`. - **`git bundle create f A..B` with two raw SHAs** makes a bundle with no refs, which git refuses as empty. The tip must be a named ref: `A..design/v2`. - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` aurora layer paints above static content.** Page content needs `relative z-[1]`. - **A `backdrop-filter` ancestor becomes the containing block for `fixed` children** — `createPortal` to `document.body` instead. - **Never size a fixed overlay from a header's height.** That is the header's bottom edge only when nothing sits above it, and the sandbox banner does. Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - ~~Do not run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`~~ — **superseded 2026-09-12.** The owner authorized running these directly from this session; see the guardrails in "Reaching node-1" above. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

I found a big clue: the main page loads over plain HTTP fine, but every asset it references afterward — CSS, JS, fonts, images — gets requested over HTTPS on that same port, which fails since port 8080 only speaks HTTP.

This is almost certainly the "Strict-Transport-Security" header (HSTS) I saw in the curl output earlier — once a browser sees that header on the initial response, it forces all future connections to that host, on any port, to HTTPS for the max-age duration, so a fresh Playwright browser context receiving it on the first load would upgrade every subsequent same-origin request, and since port 8080 has no TLS listener, they all fail with ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR. This looks like a classic misconfiguration where nginx or Next.js is sending the HSTS header even on the non-TLS staging port.

This explains the unstyled page with no JS execution — hydration never happens since it's raw server HTML — and the click-blocking overlay, since the CSS that would normally handle pointer-events never loaded. This feels like the critical bug for the whole task: HSTS on a direct-IP staging port would break the entire experience for any real browser, killing CSS, JS hydration, and interactivity across the board. I want to confirm whether this header appears on every response or just some, so I'm rechecking the earlier curl output.

The header includes includeSubDomains and is scoped to the host itself (51.79.162.96), not the specific port — per RFC 6797, HSTS applies per-hostname regardless of port, meaning any browser that once loads this site over HTTP would be forced to upgrade all future connections to that host to HTTPS, typically defaulting to port 443. That's catastrophic for staging access over a non-TLS IP:port combination if there's no reachable HTTPS endpoint to redirect to.

Checking the observed requests confirms Chrome preserved the explicitly specified port (8080) while forcing the scheme to https — so HSTS is upgrading to https on the same port, which has no TLS listener, explaining the protocol errors. Since this same IP serves both production (443, valid TLS) and staging (8080), it's likely production's HSTS header is bleeding over and breaking staging access entirely.

But testing this in a fresh Playwright context that only ever visited staging on port 8080 (never touched production/443), the same HSTS forcing still occurred — meaning the staging service itself must be setting the HSTS header directly, not inheriting it from production.
